changes: Holding FUNC while turning SIZE, DCY, ABSB or SPD now steps through 0, the centre (64) and 127, as MIX and DPTH already did and as on the stock reverbs' MIX. In 0.1.0 those four knobs jumped only between 0 and 127, an editor inherited from the stock reverb that E-Verb's page is cloned from (#438).

Plain turns and every stored value are unchanged: only four editor words in E-Verb's FX2 descriptor change. The DSP code and memory are byte-identical to 0.1.0, so the sound and cycle cost are unchanged, and the knob values a project stores mean the same.

Measured on the ColdFire emulator only: 0.1.1 has not run on hardware. The owner's MKII report (two simultaneous instances, Part/project reload, physical reboot) covers 0.1.0; MKI, full-load chip timing and broader hardware coverage remain unverified.
Documentation/media-only: add an offline audio preview rendered through 0.1.0-experimental, with sample credits, settings and provenance; firmware is unchanged.

Documentation/media-only (12 October 2026): replace the old preview with an original chord stab at dry, hall and shimmer settings, give shimmer a 7.5-second pass, match first-hit RMS and retain exact 0.1.1 DSP/source provenance. Firmware and its version are unchanged; these offline previews add no physical-hardware or performance qualification.

Documentation/media-only (12 October 2026): use Legowelt’s bright Juno 106 chord for an 11.4-second dry/long-hall/sustaining-shimmer comparison, with audible extended tails, stronger settings, 80 ms first-hit matching and no added gaps. Include pack permission, credit, excerpt/settings hashes and decoded peak validation. Firmware and hardware/performance qualification are unchanged.
First E-Verb release: original Erbe-Verb-inspired FX2 feedback-delay reverb with size, saturation/sustain, absorption, chorus/grains/shimmer, reverse pre-delay, tilt and envelope routings.
The six main-page controls support locks, LFOs, scenes and MIDI CC; SETUP controls are per Part. MIX 0 is exact dry passthrough.
Uses the shared native/browser builder; alone, replaces Spring Rev and Dark Rev while preserving Plate Rev and other stock effects.

Owner reports working MKII sound, two distinct simultaneous T1/T5 instances, Part/project save/reload and physical reboot on exact EVRB01T01. Full-load silicon timing and broader hardware modulation/recovery coverage remain unverified.
